road_detail: Before a minor buys a probationary license, the driver must pass the driving and skills tests. The road test has a driving part and a maneuverability part.
supervised_quote: Driver must complete 50 hours of driving, with at least 10 hours of night driving, in addition to the driver education requirements.
holding_quote: Driver must hold the TIPIC for at least six months.

documents.summary: Proof of full legal name, date of birth, legal presence, Social Security number, and two Ohio street-address documents is required for a compliant card.
documents.quote: Applicants must provide proof of: Full legal name Date of birth Legal presence in the US Social Security number (SSN) See more information below. Ohio street address

documents.summary: An unemancipated applicant under 18 must be accompanied by a responsible person who co-signs the permit.
documents.quote: An applicant who is a minor (Under 18 years old, and unemancipated) must be accompanied by a responsible person who is willing to assume the obligation imposed under section 4507.07 of the Ohio Revised Code . The responsible person must present identification (driver license or ID card) to co-sign for the TIPIC.

documents.summary: A driver education certificate is provided at the driving and skills test.
documents.quote: A Driver Education Certificate must be provided at time of Driving and Skills testing.

documents.summary: The completed fifty-hour affidavit is brought to the driving test.
documents.quote: Download the BMV5791 Fifty-Hour Affidavit , and bring the completed form to your Driving Test appointment

real_id_summary: Beginning May 7, 2025, a REAL ID-compliant driver license or identification card is required to board a domestic flight or enter certain federal facilities, unless the traveler uses another accepted document such as a passport.
real_id_quote: Beginning May 7, 2025 , U.S. travelers must be REAL ID compliant to board domestic flights and access certain federal facilities.
transfer_summary: An unexpired out-of-state non-commercial license can be exchanged at age 16 or older. If the out-of-state license is expired, or the person is a first-time driver, the testing process is required. The new-resident page does not say a current out-of-state license holder skips the knowledge or road test.
transfer_quote: If you are at least 16 years of age and have an unexpired out-of-state driver license (non-CDL), you can apply for an Ohio driver license.
teen_summary: A temporary instruction permit starts at 15 years and six months, after a knowledge test and vision screening. A minor must hold it at least six months, finish driver education, complete 50 hours including 10 at night, and pass the driving and skills tests. The fee schedule lists a first operator license at age 16. During the first probationary period the driver may not drive from midnight to 6 a.m. except in listed circumstances, and may not carry more than one non-family passenger unless a parent or guardian is along. A later section still applies while the driver is under 18.
teen_quote: At age 15 years and six months, an applicant may complete the knowledge test online at Ohio BMV - Online Services , or go to select deputy registrar locations or any driver exam station to take the knowledge test and vision screening, to begin the temporary permit process.

teen_points.text: Temporary permit at 15 years and six months.
teen_points.quote: At age 15 years and six months, an applicant may complete the knowledge test online at Ohio BMV - Online Services , or go to select deputy registrar locations or any driver exam station to take the knowledge test and vision screening, to begin the temporary permit process.

teen_points.text: Hold the temporary permit at least six months.
teen_points.quote: Driver must hold the TIPIC for at least six months.

teen_points.text: Fifty hours, including 10 at night, in addition to driver education.
teen_points.quote: Driver must complete 50 hours of driving, with at least 10 hours of night driving, in addition to the driver education requirements.

teen_points.text: Driver education is 24 hours of class and 8 hours of driving.
teen_points.quote: 24 hours of classroom or online instruction and 8 hours of driving time.

teen_points.text: First probationary period: no driving from midnight to 6 a.m. except listed reasons.
teen_points.quote: You may not operate a vehicle from midnight - 6 a.m. unless:

teen_points.text: No more than one non-family passenger unless a parent or guardian is along.
teen_points.quote: You may not operate a vehicle with more than one non-family member as a passenger unless accompanied by a parent or guardian.

teen_points.text: After 12 months and still under 18, the night limit becomes 1 a.m. to 5 a.m.
teen_points.quote: After the First 12 Months of Holding a License and Under Age 18 You may not operate a vehicle from 1 - 5 a.m. unless:

curfew: During the first period of a probationary license, the driver may not drive from midnight to 6 a.m. unless a parent, guardian, or other listed adult is along, or the trip is for work, school, or another exception the page lists. After 12 months, while still under 18, the night limit is 1 a.m. to 5 a.m.
curfew_quote: You may not operate a vehicle from midnight - 6 a.m. unless:
passengers: A probationary driver may not carry more than one non-family passenger unless a parent or guardian is in the vehicle.
passengers_quote: You may not operate a vehicle with more than one non-family member as a passenger unless accompanied by a parent or guardian.
gaps: The graduated-licensing page states the temporary-permit age as 15 years and six months and a six-month holding period. It does not itself say the probationary license starts at 16. The fee schedule is the page that lists a first operator license at age 16.
The BMV forms page links to a digest of motor vehicle laws, and that address returned 404, so no handbook URL is recorded.
No opened page said whether an out-of-state learner permit is accepted.
